clue.text: Country house: term for family area

parts.note: ken is old slang, from thieves' cant, for a house

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so the word after it gives up only its closing letter

parts.note: the final letter of family
A is the usual abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A note on a country house: one wing has a name for the family quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken, meaning a house, is cant from the Regency underworld and turns up regularly in barred puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya is a nation in East Africa, so it is a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: Rising wit sure to host grand assemblies

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: salt is sharp wit, as in Attic salt

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so that word takes the next piece inside

parts.note: OK, sure, all right
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A clever person on the way up is happy to entertain at large gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising wit' reads as an up-and-coming comedian; in a down entry it is an instruction to reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A kgotla is a traditional public meeting or court of elders in Botswana, a tribal gathering place.

clue.text: Blushes as Bruce's scene flops following eccentricity

indicators.note: following places the jumbled material after the single letter that comes next in the clue

parts.note: e is the mathematical symbol for the eccentricity of a conic

indicators.note: a flop collapses and falls apart, so the letters before it tumble into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone goes red with embarrassment when Bruce's oddball scene fails on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentricity' looks like Bruce's quirky behaviour, but it is the maths quantity written as e.
explanation.definitionFit: Erubescence is the act of reddening or turning red, so instances of it are flushes of the face.

clue.text: Remark about a moth spreading out

indicators.note: about here means around, so the first word surrounds the jumbled letters

parts.note: a note is a brief remark

indicators.note: spreading out means scattering, so the letters disperse into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A comment about a moth opening its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreading out' looks like a phrase, but the definition is 'out' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out is away from their house, which is what the phrase means; it was also a polite refusal to callers.

clue.text: Dragonflies chase around before going up

indicators.note: around suggests running about every which way, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the short word flips

parts.note: an, an old dialect form taken here to mean before

explanation.surface: Dragonflies dart about in pursuit before flying upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschna is a genus of large hawker dragonflies, so the name stands for these insects.

clue.text: European local found during search

indicators.note: something found during an activity sits in the middle of it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to fish for something is to search for it
your local is your nearest pub, and an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A person from elsewhere in Europe is discovered in the middle of a hunt for a nearby resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like a person living nearby; in British usage it is also your regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnish people come from Finland, a Nordic nation, so the adjective describes a kind of continental native.

clue.text: Up-to-date telly's about overturning solemn settings

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the telly pieces go around the overturned word

parts.note: FST, a flat-screen TV, the modern set

indicators.note: overturning turns something upside down, which in a down entry means reading it backwards

parts.note: po, as in po-faced, means solemn and humourless
the apostrophe-s supplies its letter

explanation.surface: A modern television's controls are flipped round from their serious settings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settings' looks like part of the telly, but it means camera aperture settings.
explanation.definitionFit: F-stops are the graded aperture positions on a camera lens, so they are photographic settings.

clue.text: Noun replacing quiet feeble sort is potty

indicators.note: replacing means taking the place of, so one letter is swapped in for another

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noun
p, piano, means quiet in music
someone who is putty in your hands is weak and easily moulded

explanation.surface: A grammatical swap turns a weak quiet person into someone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like a child's toilet; here it is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British terms for slightly mad or eccentric, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Born with money? Supplier of beneficial oil

parts.note: née, born, used before a woman's maiden name
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Someone born rich asks who provides a healthy oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The neem is a tropical tree whose seeds yield an oil used in medicine and insect repellents.

clue.text: We're inseparable as one in unchanged group comes out on top

indicators.note: one item in another goes inside it, so that letter sits within the next word

parts.note: unchanged means the same
I is the Roman numeral one
a set is a group
someone who wins comes out on top

explanation.surface: A team boasts that they stick together as one and an unchanged line-up is victorious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As one' looks like part of the unity theme, but 'one' is the numeral and 'as' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjoined twins, once called by this name after a famous pair from Siam, are physically joined and cannot separate.

clue.text: As used by poet, meat wagon is boring now

definitions.text: As used by poet, meat wagon

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the short word goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: here and now
is shortened to 's, as in it's

explanation.surface: A poet's word for a hearse is dreary these days.
explanation.walkthrough: Meat wagon is slang for a hearse or ambulance; 'boring' looks like dull but means drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Herse is an old poetic spelling of hearse, the vehicle carrying a coffin, which slang calls a meat wagon.

clue.text: ____ is leaving requisite ogres formed extravagantly

definitions.note: the blank stands for the answer itself, so the clue reads 'the answer is what is left when...'

indicators.note: shaped in a wild, extravagant way, the remaining letters are rearranged freely
leaving here means going away, so that short word departs from the longer phrase

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A self-describing riddle: some necessary monsters are given wildly overdone shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is the answer itself: take IS out of the two clue words and rearrange the rest, and the result describes those ogres.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotesquerie means grotesque things or quality, which fits monsters made in an exaggerated, distorted manner.

clue.text: Vehicle's condition in reversal of career

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside the second word
the phrase says outright that the following word is to be read from its end back to its start

parts.note: to career is to rush along, and to race is the same
a condition is a state, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: A comment on a car's condition after a reversal in someone's working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' reads as a job history, but here it is the verb meaning to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon, a type of motor vehicle with a long rear load space.

clue.text: Atmosphere in restaurant

indicators.note: the answer is literally sitting in the next word, inside its run of letters

parts.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A diner's ambience.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive feeling or air surrounding a place, which is what an atmosphere is.

clue.text: Tower possibly to be advised by King

parts.note: TBA is the abbreviation for to be advised or announced
R for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone is waiting for the monarch to tell them about a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' looks like a tall building, but it means something that tows; 'possibly' warns that it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a ski lift that drags skiers uphill, so it is one kind of thing that tows people.

clue.text: Club's polled about starter

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: polled means having the hair or horns cut off, i.e. shorn
a tiro is a beginner

explanation.surface: A society has surveyed its members about a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polled' suggests a survey and 'starter' a meal; they mean shorn and novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A short iron is a golf club with a steep face, such as a nine iron or wedge, for short approach shots.

clue.text: No longer stop children finding boggy ground

parts.note: let once meant hinder, a sense now archaic, which 'no longer' flags
CH is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: Parents give up stopping their children, who wander off and discover a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The old sense of let survives in 'without let or hindrance' and in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A letch is a wet, marshy hollow or stream, a dialect word for swampy land.

clue.text: Please pray they're exceptionally quiet at the front

indicators.note: this places the single soft-sound letter before everything else in the answer

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: doing something exceptionally means out of the ordinary way, so the letters leave their usual order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A plea that some people should be unusually silent, starting with a polite request.
explanation.definitionFit: Prythee is an old contraction of 'I pray thee', a courteous way of asking someone for something.

clue.text: Who lack conviction in Greece's capital? First couple are deported

indicators.note: deported people are sent away, so the opening two letters are expelled from the word

parts.note: the capital city of Greece

explanation.surface: A question about convicts in Athens, followed by the news that two of them have been expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conviction' suggests court verdicts; here it means firmness of mind. 'First couple' also hints at a pair of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen can mean a timid, faint-hearted person, so the plural describes those without boldness or resolve.

clue.text: Millions getting stuck into hot toast is tops

indicators.note: being stuck into something means pushed inside it, so one piece is lodged within the other
hot can mean stolen or agitated, so the word next to it is disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Crowds tucking into hot toast is the best thing going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tops' looks like praise for the toast, but it is the informal word for a maximum, as in five pounds tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Said after a figure, 'tops' means no more than that amount, which is the upper limit sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Somewhat unlikely having it for special shawl

indicators.note: having one thing for another means putting it in that other's place, so a swap is made

parts.note: a tall story is unlikely, so somewhat tall is somewhat unlikely
it shortened to 't, as in 'tis
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: An improbable story about a special shawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Tall means far-fetched, as in a tall tale; tallish softens it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallith is the fringed shawl worn by Jewish men at prayer, a ritual garment.

clue.text: Trollop grins for locals around independent Earl

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so that word wraps the single letter

parts.note: grin is a dialect word for a snare, so locals' grins are traps
I is the abbreviation for independent
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A loose woman smiles at villagers surrounding a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grins' looks like smiles; in dialect a grin is a noose or snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A traipse can be a slovenly, untidy woman, an old dialect sense of the word, matching trollop.

clue.text: Collectors of pollen range across acres

indicators.note: something stretching across another covers it from side to side, so it wraps around the short piece

parts.note: scope is range or extent
A is an abbreviation for acres

explanation.surface: Bees or similar insects roam over wide fields gathering pollen.
explanation.definitionFit: Scopae are the brush-like tufts of hair on a bee's legs or body that gather and carry pollen grains.

clue.text: Pay up for spitfire

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to ante, or ante up, is to pay one's stake

explanation.surface: A demand to settle a bill for a fighter plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spitfire' calls up the wartime fighter, but a volcano also spits fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active Sicilian volcano that erupts lava and flame, so it literally spits fire.

clue.text: Rab C's one about wife in bedroom

indicators.note: the two short pieces sit in the abbreviation that follows, so they go inside it

parts.note: BR is the estate agents' abbreviation for bedroom
W is the abbreviation for wife
a., short for about, as in an approximate date

explanation.surface: Rab C. Nesbitt tells his latest one about a wife in a bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab C. Nesbitt is a Glaswegian TV comic character, which signals a Scots word. 'One' means a joke, as in 'the one about...'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bawr is a Scots word for a joke or jest, the kind of story a Glasgow comedian tells.

clue.text: Pigeon bit first marsh-dweller

indicators.note: first puts the piece it follows at the front, ahead of the bird's word

parts.note: taken as written
tur is the pigeon pea, a tropical legume

explanation.surface: A pigeon was the first to bite a creature from the marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pigeon' looks like the bird; it is the pigeon pea, an Indian pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Bittur is an old spelling of bittern, a wading heron that lives among reeds in wetlands.

clue.text: Local population name child who does the chasing over denial

parts.note: a deme is a local population, originally a district of ancient Attica

parts.note: in the game of tag the chaser is called 'it'

explanation.surface: Locals name the child who chases in the playground, despite a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: Deme is used in biology too, for a local group of interbreeding organisms.

clue.text: One on benefit spotted cat climbing curtain

pard is an old word for a leopard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like noticed; it describes the leopard's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a long heavy curtain, the usual American word for one.

clue.text: In a worthy way, awkwardly only involving Baron

indicators.note: involving means wrapping up within, so the shuffled word encloses the title letter
done awkwardly, the word is clumsily rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for baron

clue.text: Attorney left backing worm

clue.text: Wind leads to bloating — offensive release assured

indicators.note: leads are the front runners, so only the opening letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface describes intestinal wind; the answer is a weather wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The bora is a cold, gusty north-easterly that blows down onto the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Equipment mostly with current ground worker

parts.note: kit is equipment

I is the symbol for electric current

clue.text: American chap I see clutching mug like a tumbler?

taken as written
the letter C is spoken like 'see'

clue.text: Busy butlers on tap, these define some kings

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: I try Pope or one of his ilk

clue.text: League's first use of anything not involving line
